meta.description: Graphify vs no-Graphify token cost. For each question the graph answers in one compact query_graph call; the 'no graph' baseline is the source files that query's answer nodes come from - i.e. the code an agent would have to read to answer the same question. That baseline is generous to the no-graph side: it assumes the agent already knows exactly which files to open, which is itself what the graph provides. Regenerate query set as needed; ratios depend on the ORE checkout (ORE_ENGINE). s01-s08 are the original suite (kept unchanged for history); s09-s50 widen coverage to every merged chunk and vary mode/depth/phrasing, added to catch term-weight drift outside the trade-pricing core the original 8 focus on (see CLAUDE.md rule 3). A question also carries a rubric, since token cost alone cannot tell a better answer from a cheaper wrong one. `required_nodes` is what the answer must contain and gates the command; `xfail_nodes` is what it should contain but does not yet, which is reported and never gates, so a half-right question still protects its working half. Entries are `label`, `label@source-file` (labels match whole, so `Swap` is not satisfied by `SwapIndex`), or `src:<path fragment>` for questions about a body of code rather than a symbol. Both lists state the answer a domain reader would expect; only the split between them reflects what the graph does today, so moving an entry from `xfail_nodes` to `required_nodes` is how an improvement gets locked in. A rubric naming a `fieldmap/...` path is skipped when the graph was merged without a fieldmap snapshot. s51-s64 cover the cross-domain fieldmap links, docs, xsd and tests; their expectations were drafted from the source (ORE_Forge data, C++, xsd/, Docs/, test dirs) before any was run, and each carries a `why`. A question may also carry `variants` (paraphrases graded against the same rubric; one that misses a required node gates), `xfail_variants` (paraphrases known to fail; reported, never gate, each needs a `why`), `controls` (unrelated questions of the same shape: a required node that also answers one is weak) and `why` (entry -> reason; required for every entry from meta.why_required_from on). See docs/BENCH.md.
